subject: Scam alert: the "package on hold" text
preheader: A $1.99 redelivery fee is how they get your card. Track packages in the shipper's app instead.
html:
A $1.99 redelivery fee is how they get your card. Track packages in the shipper's app instead.
Scam warning · Scam of the week · 2026-11-24

"Your package is on hold" texts are spiking before Black Friday

Arrives by: text · From: a delivery company, from a number you don't know (fictional example)

USPS: Your package is on hold due to an incomplete address. Update within 12 hours and pay a $1.99 redelivery fee: usps-redeliver-help.com

3 tells

  1. A text you didn't sign up for, from a regular phone number, about a package you can't name.
  2. A tiny fee and a short deadline. The fee is the bait; the page wants your full card details.
  3. A link that only looks like the shipper's site. The real domain is right before the first single slash.

Do this

  1. Don't tap. Track packages in the shipper's app or by typing its website yourself.
  2. Expecting something? Check the order page on the store's own site or app.
  3. Forward the text to 7726 (SPAM), then delete it.

Already clicked, paid or shared? Typed your card number? Call the number on the back of your card and ask for a new one. Then watch your statement for small test charges.

subject: Scam alert: the "your account was in the breach" call
preheader: Your bank won't ask you to read out a code. Hang up and call the number on your card.
html:
Your bank won't ask you to read out a code. Hang up and call the number on your card.
Watch for this · Scam of the week · 2026-12-08

Fake "fraud team" calls after a data breach

Arrives by: call · From: your bank's "fraud department" (fictional example)

Hi, this is the fraud team at your bank. Your account was included in the recent data breach. To secure it, please read me the 6-digit code we just sent you.

3 tells

  1. It arrives right after breach news, and uses that news to sound believable.
  2. It asks for a one-time code, a password or a PIN. That code signs them in as you.
  3. It's urgent, and it wants you to stay on the line rather than call back.

Do this

  1. Hang up and call the number on your card or statement.
  2. Work through our free data breach checklist at scamdecoded.netlify.app/breached: passwords, two-step sign-in, a credit freeze.
  3. Report the call at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

Already clicked, paid or shared? Read out a code? Change that account's password now from a device you trust, turn on two-step sign-in, and call the bank on the number on your card.

subject: Scam alert: the $6.99 "unpaid toll" text
preheader: Toll agencies bill through your account or by mail. Don't tap the link.
html:
Toll agencies bill through your account or by mail. Don't tap the link.
Urgent scam alert · Scam of the week · 2027-01-12

"Unpaid toll" texts are back

Arrives by: text · From: a toll agency, from a number or email address you don't know (fictional example)

NOTICE: You have an outstanding toll balance of $6.99. To avoid a $50 late fee and license suspension, pay by 11:59 PM today: ezdrive-tollpay.top

3 tells

  1. A small amount with a big threat attached: late fees, license suspension, today.
  2. A link that isn't your toll agency's real website, often with an odd ending like .top or .xyz.
  3. It arrives as a text from a number you don't know, sometimes even if you haven't driven a toll road.

Do this

  1. Don't tap. Log in to your toll account by typing the agency's website yourself, or call the number on your statement.
  2. Check the real balance there. No balance? It's fake.
  3. Forward the text to 7726 (SPAM), and report it at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

Already clicked, paid or shared? Paid on that page? Call your card company today, ask for a new card, and dispute the charge.

Toll text scams come in waves. If one reaches you this week, it's likely reaching your parents too: forward them this alert.
